submissions.findingTextShort: PMID 17470980 is an esophageal-temperature catheter-ablation phantom study and cannot support Chondroitin osteoarthritis evidence.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: The current NOINDEX Chondroitin profile uses PMID 17470980, an experimental esophageal-temperature monitoring study involving a radiofrequency catheter-ablation agar phantom model. It does not study chondroitin supplementation or osteoarthritis and therefore cannot support Chondroitin efficacy, human-study count, or evidence grade. The same unrelated source also appears in Glucosamine, suggesting a shared evidence-join defect rather than an independent scientific citation.
submissions.usageContext: Source-integrity defect only; no chondroitin intervention is present.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Bibliographic mismatch is direct. Research staging records the defect without mutating the canonical source edge.

submissions.findingTextShort: A 2024 knee-OA meta-analysis evaluates glucosamine sulfate, chondroitin sulfate, and combination regimens; intervention identity must remain separated.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A 2024 systematic review/meta-analysis of knee-osteoarthritis trials evaluates glucosamine sulfate, chondroitin sulfate and combination regimens. It provides a modern evidence anchor but cannot be summarized as one undifferentiated Chondroitin effect: chondroitin-alone, glucosamine-alone and combination findings require separate claim roles, and symptomatic outcomes should not be converted into structural disease-modification claims.
submissions.populationContext: Adults with knee osteoarthritis represented across randomized trials in a systematic review/meta-analysis.
submissions.usageContext: Chondroitin sulfate, glucosamine sulfate and combination OA regimens; intervention-role separation required.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Mixed intervention classes and trial heterogeneity constrain isolated-chondroitin inference.

submissions.findingTextShort: A knee-OA meta-analysis of glucosamine plus chondroitin is combination evidence and cannot establish Chondroitin's isolated contribution.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A systematic review/meta-analysis evaluates combined glucosamine plus chondroitin treatment in knee osteoarthritis. Any pooled symptomatic signal belongs to the combination intervention and must not be attributed solely to chondroitin. Product quality, preparation, duration and symptomatic versus structural outcomes remain material boundaries.
submissions.populationContext: Adults with knee osteoarthritis represented in combination-treatment trials.
submissions.usageContext: Glucosamine plus chondroitin combination therapy; not isolated Chondroitin monotherapy.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Combination evidence cannot isolate the independent effect of Chondroitin.

submissions.findingTextShort: Additional glucosamine-chondroitin combination evidence reinforces the need for an isolated-versus-combination attribution firewall.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A 2022 clinical evidence synthesis of glucosamine/chondroitin combination treatment reinforces that much of the accessible osteoarthritis literature evaluates the ingredients together. Future Chondroitin promotion needs explicit intervention-role tagging so combination outcomes cannot silently inflate isolated-chondroitin efficacy or grade.
submissions.usageContext: Combination osteoarthritis evidence used as an attribution-boundary research receipt.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: This source is useful primarily for intervention-role governance; it does not independently prove isolated Chondroitin efficacy.
